headline: NiSource, the utility group behind the Northern Indiana Public Service Company, has signed a 20-year deal to supply electricity to a Microsoft data centre campus in Indiana.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a signed 20-year supply deal announced by both companies, with a customer-protection structure, but a single regional deal.
importance_line: Electricity customers in northern Indiana are promised protection from data-centre costs and projected savings, and Microsoft secures long-term power from 2028, though the savings figure is NiSource's own expectation.
summary: Dow Jones Newswires reports that NiSource and Microsoft said on 16 Oct 2026 that Microsoft will take electric service for its Indiana data centre campus under a 20-year term starting in 2028 and will fully fund the generation and infrastructure needed to serve it, so that existing customers of the Northern Indiana Public Service Company are protected from added costs. NiSource expects total customer savings of about 1.75 billion dollars over the life of all its data centre contracts, up from a previous projection of 1.4 billion dollars.
notes: Read in full on Morningstar, which carries Dow Jones Newswires text; Dow Jones is credited as the reporter. Savings are the company's projection.
